translations.idiomatic: Two great chieftains, Mohedagan and Dumodu, commanded the most powerful tribes.

sentences.zh: 百姓又分為黃姓、黑姓兩種，互相猜阻。

translations.literal: The common people were again divided into Yellow Surname and Black Surname, mutually suspicious and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: The people were also divided into Yellow Surname and Black Surname factions, mutually suspicious and hostile.

sentences.zh: 二十六年夏，莫賀達幹勒兵夜攻蘇祿，殺之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year Mohedagan led troops by night to attack Sulu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year Mohedagan led a night attack on Sulu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 都摩度初與莫賀達幹連謀，俄又相背，立蘇祿之子咄火仙為可汗，以輯其余眾，與莫賀達幹自相攻擊。

translations.literal: Dumodu at first joined in plotting with Mohedagan; soon they turned against each other; he set up Sulu's son Tuohuoxian as qaghan to gather the remaining masses, and they attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Dumodu had first plotted with Mohedagan but soon turned against him; he set up Sulu's son Tuohuoxian as qaghan to rally the survivors, and the two fought each other.

sentences.zh: 莫賀達幹遣使告安西都護蓋嘉運。

translations.literal: Mohedagan sent envoys to inform Protector-General of Anxi Gai Jiayun.
translations.idiomatic: Mohedagan sent envoys to inform Protector-General of Anxi Gai Jiayun.

sentences.zh: 嘉運率兵討之，大敗都摩度之眾，臨陣擒咄火仙，並收得金河公主而還。

translations.literal: Jiayun led troops to campaign against him, greatly defeated Dumodu's masses, captured Tuohuoxian on the battlefield, and also took Princess of Jinhe and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun led troops against him, routed Dumodu's forces, captured Tuohuoxian on the field, and took Princess of Jinhe back with him.

sentences.zh: 又欲立史懷道之子昕為可汗以鎮撫之，莫賀達幹不肯，曰：「討平蘇祿，本是我之元謀，若立史昕為主，則國家何以酬賞於我？

translations.literal: He also wished to set up Shi Huaidao's son Xin as qaghan to pacify and reassure them; Mohedagan would not agree, saying, "Campaigning to pacify Sulu was originally my primary plan—if Shi Xin is set up as ruler, how will the state reward me?
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to set up Shi Huaidao's son Xin as qaghan to pacify the tribes; Mohedagan refused, saying, "Pacifying Sulu was my plan from the start—if Shi Xin is made ruler, how will the court reward me?

sentences.zh: 」乃不立史昕，便令莫賀達幹統眾。

translations.literal: " He thereupon did not set up Shi Xin and ordered Mohedagan to command the masses.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not set up Shi Xin and ordered Mohedagan to command the tribes.

sentences.zh: 二十七年二月，嘉運率將士詣闕獻俘，玄宗禦花萼樓以宴之，仍令將吐火仙獻於太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year Jiayun led officers and soldiers to court to present captives; Xuanzong attended at Hua'e Tower to feast them and also ordered Tuohuoxian presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year Jiayun led his officers to court with captives; Xuanzong feasted them at Hua'e Tower and ordered Tuohuoxian presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 俄又黃姓、黑姓自相屠殺，各遣使降附。

translations.literal: Soon the Yellow Surname and Black Surname again slaughtered one another and each sent envoys to surrender and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Yellow and Black Surnames slaughtered one another again, and each faction sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：中原多事，外國窺邊，周獫狁、漢匈奴之後，其類實繁，前史論之備矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: The central plains had many affairs; foreign states peered at the borders; after the Xianyun of Zhou and the Xiongnu of Han, their kinds were truly numerous—the former histories have discussed this fully.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: When the central plains were troubled, foreign peoples watched the borders; after the Xianyun of Zhou and the Xiongnu of Han, their kinds multiplied—the former histories have discussed this fully.

sentences.zh: 突厥自隋文修王道，肅軍容，示恩威以羈縻之；

translations.literal: The Turks, from the time when Emperor Wen of Sui cultivated the kingly way, disciplined military appearance, and displayed grace and might to bind and restrain them;
translations.idiomatic: From the time Emperor Wen of Sui cultivated the kingly way, disciplined the army, and displayed grace and might to bind the Turks;

sentences.zh: 煬帝失政教，生戎心，肇亂離以啟發之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang lost proper government and teaching, bred a martial heart, and began disorder and separation to stir them up.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang lost proper governance, bred martial ambition, and through disorder stirred them to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高祖借其力而入平京師，群賊附其強而叠據河朔。

translations.literal: Gaozu borrowed their strength to enter and pacify the capital; bandits attached to their power and repeatedly held the north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu borrowed their strength to take the capital; rebels attached to their power and repeatedly held the north.

sentences.zh: 高祖同禦榻以延其使，太宗幸便橋以約其和。

translations.literal: Gaozu shared the imperial couch to receive their envoys; Taizong went to Bian Bridge to secure peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu shared his couch to receive their envoys; Taizong went to Bian Bridge to secure peace with them.

sentences.zh: 當其時焉，不其盛矣！

translations.literal: In those times—was it not their zenith!
translations.idiomatic: In those days—was it not their zenith!

sentences.zh: 竟滅其族而身死於國者，何也？

translations.literal: Yet in the end their clans were extinguished and they themselves died in our state—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end their clans were extinguished and they died in our realm—why?

sentences.zh: 咸謂太宗有馭夷狄之道，李勣著戡定之功。

translations.literal: All say Taizong had the way of controlling the barbarians, and Li Ji achieved the merit of pacification by force.
translations.idiomatic: All say Taizong had the art of controlling the barbarians, and Li Ji achieved the merit of pacification by force.

sentences.zh: 殊不知突厥之始也，賞罰明而將士戮力。

translations.literal: They do not realize that at the Turks' beginning rewards and punishments were clear and officers and soldiers exerted their strength together.
translations.idiomatic: They do not realize that at the Turks' beginning rewards and punishments were clear and officers and soldiers fought as one.

sentences.zh: 遇煬帝之亂，亡命蓄怒者既附之，其興也宜哉！

translations.literal: When they met the disorder of Emperor Yang, fugitives storing up wrath all attached to them—their rise was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang's disorder came, fugitives nursing grievances flocked to them—their rise was inevitable!

sentences.zh: 頡利之衰也，兄弟扌勾隙而部族離心。

translations.literal: At Jieli's decline, brothers quarreled and tribes lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: At Jieli's decline, brothers quarreled and the tribes lost heart.

sentences.zh: 當太宗之理，謀臣猛將討逐之，其亡也宜哉！

translations.literal: When Taizong governed, strategists and fierce generals pursued and expelled them—their fall was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong's rule, strategists and fierce generals pursued and expelled them—their fall was inevitable!

sentences.zh: 洎武後亂朝，默啜犯塞，玄宗纂嗣，傳首京師，東封太山，西戎扈蹕，開元之代，繼踵來降。

translations.literal: Down to the disorderly court of Empress Wu, Mochuo raided the frontier; Xuanzong succeeded to the throne, heads were sent to the capital, he enfeoffed Mount Tai in the east, western Rong escorted his carriage, and in the Kaiyuan era they came in succession to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Through Empress Wu's troubled reign Mochuo raided the frontier; Xuanzong succeeded, enemy heads reached the capital, he performed the eastern feng on Mount Tai, western tribes escorted his progress, and in the Kaiyuan era they surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 西突厥諸族，遇其理，則眾心悅附而甲兵興焉；

translations.literal: The various clans of the Western Turks—when they met good governance, hearts rejoiced and submitted and arms flourished;
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk clans—under good governance hearts submitted and arms flourished;

sentences.zh: 遇其亂，則族類怨怒而本根破矣！

translations.literal: when they met disorder, clans resented in anger and the root was broken!
translations.idiomatic: under disorder clans turned resentful and their foundations collapsed!

sentences.zh: 理亂二道，華夷一途。

translations.literal: The two paths of order and disorder are one road for Chinese and barbarian alike.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder follow the same law for Chinese and barbarian alike.

sentences.zh: 或質言於盛衰倚伏，未為確論。

translations.literal: To speak plainly of rise and fall, waxing and waning, is not yet a settled judgment.
translations.idiomatic: To speak only of rise and fall in terms of fortune is not yet a settled judgment.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：中國失政，邊夷幸災。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When China lost proper government, frontier barbarians rejoiced at the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: When China lost proper government, frontier peoples rejoiced at the disaster.

sentences.zh: 理亂之道，取鑒將來。

translations.literal: The way of order and disorder—take it as a mirror for what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: The way of order and disorder—let it be a mirror for the future.
